reason: Conversation 1 gives an honest, well-weighted differential (start relay most likely, airflow/overheating, possibly a tired compressor), asks the two most useful questions (age, compressor temperature), then sets out a sensible sequence: unplugged condenser clean and ventilation, monitor, cheap relay gamble, engineer to measure compressor current, and a realistic repair-vs-replace verdict at 10 years, plus food-safety advice. Conversation 2 loops on an unperformed visual inspection, never mentions an engineer or cost ceiling, and ends with fabricated and unsafe-leaning advice to 'turn the compressor shaft by hand' via a 'central bolt or pulley' - hermetic fridge compressors have no accessible shaft, so this would mislead the homeowner into prodding at the sealed unit. Conversation 1's only minor wobble is listing a control board as a low-probability cause, which is appropriately hedged.
